lines: +description: "Check which movies, sound files, pictures and LUTs Frame Job can bring in, what happens to transparency, rotation and odd frame rates, and which way in takes which file."
+This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).
+  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
+| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
+| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
+| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
+Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
+Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
+| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
+| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, through macOS's optional decoder. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
+| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |

+Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
+The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
+Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
+A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
+A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
+Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track, which gives a variable-rate file one rate too.

+A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
+If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.

+macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
+A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
+M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.

+Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.

+Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
+This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
+PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
+A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
+Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
+| The still is | What Frame Job does |
+| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
+| Labelled HLG or PQ | Treats it by its own colour instead of as SDR. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
+| HEIC with an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's) | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
+A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
+Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
+- 3D only, so a 1D LUT is refused.
+A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.
+An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
+Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
+The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
+| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
+| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
+| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
+| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
+| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

+A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
+In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.
+description: Every mouse and trackpad gesture on the timeline, the preview canvas and the Color tab, with the modifier keys that change what it does.
+Much of Frame Job's editing is direct: you drag, click and pinch rather than choose a command. This page lists those gestures by where you make them, with the modifier keys that change them.
+  where={['The timeline', 'The preview canvas', 'The Media tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
+On the timeline and the canvas, every drag is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it. A click that doesn't move anything adds no step.
+| Click | A clip | Selects it alone. Clicking a clip that's already in a multi-selection keeps the selection, so you can drag it. |
+| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | A clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
+| Click | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Deselects everything. |
+| Drag | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Draws a marquee that selects every clip it touches. |
+| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag | The same places | Draws a marquee that adds to the selection. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click | A track header | Selects every clip on that track. |
+A marquee skips clips on locked tracks, but a click can still select one. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
+| Drag | A clip | Moves the selected clips, in time and to other tracks. A selection across several tracks keeps its spacing. |
+| Drag | Past the top or bottom track | Puts the clips on a new track: a new front track above the top, a new back track below the bottom. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip | Duplicates the clips and moves the copies. The whole selection is copied when the clip is in it. |
+The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, and the others keep their offsets. A linked partner moves by the same time, but a sound half dragged to its own track goes there alone.
+Dragging a clip onto its neighbour on the same track makes a Cross Dissolve across the overlap, within the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).

+During a drag the clip skips positions the project won't allow and waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts. If the drop can't go where you let go, a ghost of the clip animates back to where it belongs. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
+| Drag | A clip's edge | [Trims](/editing/trimming/) that edge. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip's end edge | [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/): changes the speed so the clip fills the new length. |
+| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's body | [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the source under the clip while the clip stays. |
+| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's edge | [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the cut between this clip and the clip touching it. |

+**Trim.** The edge zone is 7 pt wide, and the pointer turns into the resize cursor over it. A clip 21 pt wide or less is all body, so zoom in to trim it. A trim keeps at least one frame and stays within the source file. Dragging the edge of a linked sound half moves it alone and leaves its picture, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).

+**Rate stretch** works only on a clip that plays a media file. On any other clip, and on a start edge, <kbd>⌥</kbd> trims as usual. Nothing happens past the speed limits of ×0.1 and ×1000, or under one frame, and Frame Job won't stretch a linked clip.
+**Slip** never snaps, moves a frame at a time and doesn't change the selection. A linked partner on an unlocked track slips with the clip.
+**Roll** does nothing where no clip touches that edge, so not over a gap or a transition. Each clip keeps at least one frame, and a roll snaps as a trim does.
+Clips on a locked track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled.
+| Drag | A fade handle | Sets that clip's audio [fade](/audio/fades/) in or out. |
+| Drag | The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) on a clip | Changes the level in force there, in dB, shown beside the pointer. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | The volume line | Adds a volume point there as an action, then sets its level. |

+A fade handle is the small square at the top corner of a clip's audio area. It lands on whole frames, can't go past the clip's length and doesn't snap to clip edges. It doesn't work on a locked track.

+The volume line grabs within 3 pt and drags up and down only. Its scale runs from +30.1 dB at the top to −60 dB, and the very bottom is silence, shown as −∞ dB. Inside or after an action that names volume, the drag edits that action's end. Anywhere else it edits the clip's volume.
+Adding a point beeps inside an action that also changes something else, and less than a frame after the previous action's end.
+A <kbd>⇧</kbd>-press or a double-click on the line acts on the clip instead, so selecting, slipping and renaming still work there.
+| Click | An action band | Selects the clip and that action, and parks the playhead at the action's end. The Clip tab then edits the action's end values. |
+| Drag | An action band | Moves the action in time, on whole frames. It stops at the next action and at the clip's own length. |
+| Drag | The edge of a band, its outer 5 pt | Changes the action's start or length, keeping at least one frame. |
+<kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects the action. A band 15 pt wide or less has no edge zones and is all body.

+While you drag, a dashed ghost marks the old place and a readout shows the new times and offset, or the change in length in frames. An action with no length can be selected but not dragged. On a locked track, a click on a band selects only the clip.
+The action lane in the Clip tab moves and resizes bands the same way, and its **Clip** chip deselects the action. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
+| Double-click | A clip | Renames it in place. |
+| Double-click | A nest clip | Goes inside the nest. To rename a nest clip, use <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>. |
+| Double-click | An empty part of a lane | [Closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). It beeps when there's no gap. It doesn't work above or below the lanes, where no track is named. |
+| Click | The breadcrumb in the corner, while a nest is open | Comes back out by one level. |
+| Click or drag | The ruler | Moves the playhead and pauses, playing the sound under it in short grains. |
+| Double-click | A marker | Renames it. <kbd>⎋</kbd> keeps the old name, and an empty name is dropped. |
+The ruler is the only way to [hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/). The transport keys and clicks on a marker move the playhead in silence.
+A marker grabs within 6 pt of its flag and snaps. Dropping it on another marker's time puts it back. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
+| Drag a header | Moves the track up or down the stack. |
+| Double-click a header | Renames the track. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a header | Selects every clip on the track. |
+| Click the sliders | Opens the track's [mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). The sliders are lit when the track's volume or pan isn't at its default. |
+Right-clicking a header gives you a menu. See [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/).

+While [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) is on (<kbd>N</kbd>), moving, trimming and rolling clips, dragging a marker and scrubbing the ruler snap to clip edges, markers, the start and end of the timeline, the playhead and the in and out points. They snap within about 8 points of the pointer at every zoom, and a guide line shows the snap. A slip doesn't snap. Every edit lands on the frame grid either way.
+Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag to turn snapping off for that drag, even if you press it partway through. It changes nothing that's remembered.
+| Pinch, or <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> with the scroll wheel | Anywhere on the timeline | Zooms around the pointer, keeping the time under it in place. |
+| Scroll | Anywhere on the timeline | Scrolls. The track headers and the ruler stay in place. |
+The zoom runs from 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, and the default is 42. During playback the timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view.

+The timeline's zoom has no menu item or shortcut except <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, which fits the whole project. The timeline bar has its own zoom controls. See [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/).
+| Drag | Drop on | What it does |
+| A row from the Media tab | A track | Places the clip at the drop point. A drop that would overlap another clip doesn't go in. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd> and a Media row | A track | [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/): makes room by pushing later clips along. |
+| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> and a Media row | A track | [Overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/): replaces what's in the way. |
+| A Media row | The preview canvas | Places the clip on a new top track at the playhead. |
+| Files from the Finder | The Media tab | Adds them to the project. |
+| Files from the Finder | Anywhere else in the window | Opens each one as its own document, the same as dropping it on the Dock icon. |
+| Files from the Finder | The Welcome window | Opens each one as its own document. |
+Only the modifier keys you hold at the drop count.
+A LUT row in the Media tab doesn't drag. Apply a LUT with **Clip ▸ Look ▸** or the Color tab. A drag between two open projects does nothing.
+| Click a clip | Selects the front-most visible clip there. |
+| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
+| Click empty canvas | Deselects everything and leaves crop mode. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, it keeps the selection. |
+| Drag a clip | Moves the selected clips by the same amount. |
+The selected clip's handles win over any clip under them. Clips on locked tracks don't move and can't be clicked, and neither can clips on hidden tracks.

+A drag [snaps](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) to the canvas centre, edges and thirds and to other layers' edges and centres, within 8 points at any zoom, with guide lines. <kbd>N</kbd> turns this off, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> suspends it, even partway through a drag.
+When an action is selected, a drag sets the value at that action's end, not the clip's own value.
+| Drag a corner or side handle | Scales, with the opposite handle pinned. Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips always scale uniformly. |
+| <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a handle | Scales around the centre. |
+| Drag the rotation handle | Rotates about the clip's uncropped centre. |
+| <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you rotate | Snaps to 15° steps. |
+| Drag a crop handle, in crop mode | Crops, without shifting what's left. A ghost shows the uncropped picture. |
+| Double-click any clip other than text | Turns on [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). |
+Scale is held from 0.01 to 10. A crop always leaves at least one source pixel.
+Shapes and text have handles of their own:
+- **On a shape,** <kbd>⇧</kbd> on a corner handle frees the aspect ratio, and a side handle changes only the width or the height. The box is held from 4 to 20,000.
+- **On a text clip,** the left and right handles set the wrap width. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly.
+| Drag a line or arrow endpoint | Moves that end of the [shape](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/). The box doesn't change. |
+| Drag an [obscure](/effects/obscure/) region's centre grip | Moves that region. |
+| Drag one of its eight handles | Resizes the region. <kbd>⌥</kbd> resizes it around its centre. |
+| Double-click a text clip | [Edits the text in place](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/), with the text selected and in the clip's own font. |

+A region's side is held from 1 to 20,000 source pixels. The grips show only with exactly one unlocked clip selected, outside crop mode. A drag inside the region but away from the grips still moves the clip.
+The text editor stays upright on a rotated clip.
+| Pinch, or <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> with the scroll wheel | Steps the canvas zoom through **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** and **200%**. |
+| Scroll | Pans a canvas that's larger than the preview. It does nothing while the canvas fits. |
+| Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag | Pans a zoomed canvas that's larger than the preview. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
+Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a wheel, a strip or a curve point to move at a tenth of the speed.
+| Strip under a wheel | Press the knob | Grabs it. |
+| Strip under a wheel | Press elsewhere | Jumps there. With <kbd>⌥</kbd>, it drags from the current value without jumping. |
+| [Curve](/color/curves/) | Click or double-click an empty part of the plot | Adds a point and drags it. |
+| Curve | <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag | Keeps the point on one axis, the one it moved most along after 4 pt of travel. |
+| Curve | Double-click a point | Removes it. |
+| Selected curve point | <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Removes it. |
+| Selected curve point | The arrow keys | Nudge it. A tone curve steps by 0.01, or 0.1 with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. A hue curve steps 1° across, or 10° with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
+| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) strip | Drag a knob | Sets that edge of the range. |
+| Qualifier strip | Drag a square | Sets the softness. |
+| Qualifier strip | Drag the body | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps around. |
+| [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) | Click a zoom cell | Changes its zoom, on the first click even when the window isn't active. |

+A curve holds up to 16 points and at least two, and it beeps past either limit. A point stays between its neighbours. Hovering over the plot shows the input and output at the pointer. To reset a whole curve, use the **Reset** item for its channel in the channel strip's menu. See [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/).
+A qualifier range that's off ignores a press.

lines: A person at the Mac can pause, resume and stop an agent's recording from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu. A pause shortens what's recorded, because `seconds` is wall-clock time, and a stop ends it early and it still lands.

-**It never asks for a grant.** The Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring grants must already be held, and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane. The recorder panel is where a person gives them. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). Frame Job started from a shell runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's.

+**It never asks for a grant.** The Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring grants must already be held, and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane. The recorder panel is where a person gives them. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). Frame Job started from a shell runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) can't use this tool, so it's for a client connected over MCP.

It checks in a fixed order: your own arguments with the Microphone and Input Monitoring grants first, then the camera, its format and the Camera grant, then the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window. A locked console or sleeping displays are refused as that, by name. An unknown camera or format is refused naming what's there.

| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
- Two media entries for one file share a single copy.

-**Reveal in Timeline** answers "where did I use this?". It selects every clip showing the file, scrolls to the earliest one, and the inspector switches to the Clip tab. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is.

+**Reveal in Timeline** answers "where did I use this?". It selects every clip showing the file and scrolls to the earliest one. If that changes the selection, the inspector switches to the Clip tab. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is.

The item is off when nothing in the timeline itself uses the file, and that includes a file whose only clips are inside a nest. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> first: the command looks at whatever's open, so it then finds the clips in there.
The new file is read as an import reads it:

-- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The file stays missing either way.

+- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The entry stays as it was either way.
- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.

- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.
+description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
+The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).
+Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.

+An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.
+A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.
+Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.
+| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
+| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
+| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels |
+Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.
+Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
+| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
+| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
+| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
+| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |
+A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

+[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.
+| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
+| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
+| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
+Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
+With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 22 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
+| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
+| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
+| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |

+The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.
+A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.
+AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
+Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.
+A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
+| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
+| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |
+An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.
+The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
+[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.
+| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
+| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
+| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
+| Master limiter | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
+| 24-bit sound | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
+| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |
+[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.
+On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.
+Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
+| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |
+| Files watched one by one | The first 16 module, font and picture files |
+| [Memory for drawn frames](/graphics/playback-and-memory/) | A quarter of the Mac's memory |
+In a folder with more than 16 files, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
+- A [camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) records at one of its formats, at that format's highest frame rate.
+- The panel offers five [camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/), and a corner layout is always the bottom-right one.
+- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.
+- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the menu-bar item was sized for.

#!/bin/zsh -i
# Each global command must still resolve and run, in an interactive shell like the owner's.
for tool in pnpm yarn gemini devcontainer drizzle-kit mmdc ncu tessl yo license-checker howdo indiana slack-shaker sprite-miner thresher live-coding-music-mcp; do
  where=$(command -v "$tool" 2>/dev/null)
  if [[ -z "$where" ]]; then
    echo "MISSING  $tool"
    continue
  fi
  real=$(readlink -f "$where" 2>/dev/null)
  out=$(perl -e 'alarm 12; exec @ARGV' "$tool" --version 2>&1 </dev/null | grep -v -E 'netrc' | tail -1 | cut -c1-60)
  echo "$tool  ${${where:h}:t}  [$out]"
done

Node comes from mise: `~/.config/mise/config.toml` has `node = "22"`, meaning the newest 22.x installed (22.23.4 since 2026-11-04; 22.18.0 kept). `.node-version` files are NOT read here: `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools` is `[]`.

**Global npm tools live inside each Node version** (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/<v>/`), including `pnpm`/`yarn` (corepack shims) and `npm link`ed personal tools (`howdo`, `indiana`, `slack-shaker`, `sprite-miner`, `thresher`), and there is no default-packages file. A plain `mise install` of a newer 22.x repoints the `22` symlink and drops them all from PATH. Copy `lib/node_modules/*` (not `npm`, `corepack`) and the `bin/` symlinks across; the links are relative and the depth matches, and native addons are fine within a major (same ABI). Never `mise upgrade` without that: it may also remove the old version a running dev server uses.

`howdo` has been unrunnable since before this: its `dist/index.js` lacks the execute bit. Related: [[target-mac-memory]] is the other host fact.

lines: +description: "Every command and submenu in the Clip menu, with its shortcut and what has to be true for it to be available."

+The Clip menu holds the commands that act on the selected clips. This page gives every item's exact title and shortcut, and what makes it available, so you can find a key or work out why something is greyed out.
+The symbols and the **(key)** mark are explained in [How to read these tables](/reference/menus/#how-to-read-these-tables). Every item here is greyed out while a sheet is on the window.
+From top to bottom, with lines dividing it into five groups after **Trim End to Playhead**, **Switch Angle ▸**, **Add Blurred Background** and **Label ▸**:
+Most items have no key, because every bare letter belongs to the editor and a menu key with no modifier would take it.
+| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |

+| **Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | Cuts the selected clips at the playhead. With nothing selected, it cuts every unlocked clip under the playhead. See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/). | The timeline has any clip |

+| **Split at Shot Changes** | | Cuts each selected clip of a video file at every hard cut in the part it plays, as one undo step. The Analyzing sheet shows while the cuts are found on this Mac. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/). | A selected clip shows a video file's picture |

+| **Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' starts to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
+| **Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' ends to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. | A selected clip is under the playhead |

+| **Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> | Holds the frame under the playhead as a still clip, 2 s long, in a gap opened there. It acts on the first selected clip under the playhead, and only on a media clip. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |

+| **Close Gap** | | Closes the gap under the playhead on the current track, and everything from the far side slides left across every unlocked track. See [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/). | The timeline has clips |
+| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
+| **Detach Audio** | <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> | Moves a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below, linked to it. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | Something is selected |
+| **Attach Audio** | <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd> | Merges a detached sound back into its picture. | A selected clip is linked to its detached sound or picture |

+| **Normalize** | | Sets the selected clips' volume to a loudness (the default, turning a clip's limiter on when its peaks need it) or a peak, by the mode chosen in the Volume section's Normalize row. A clip with processing is measured through it under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |

+| **Enhance Voice** | | Sets the selected clips up for speech from their own measurements, as one undo step. See [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |

+| **Match Audio…** | | Gives the selected clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, chosen in a sheet, measured under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |

+| **Synchronize Audio** | | Lines up the selected clips by their sound. A weak match asks you first. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |

+| **Switch by Speaker…** | | Cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as one undo step. Run **Synchronize Audio** first. See [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/). | The selected clips with a picture sit on two or more tracks and a selected clip has its sound on. It works inside a nest |
+| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |

+| **Add Action** | <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> | Adds an action at the playhead, 1 s long with an empty end state. Frame Job won't add one that would overlap another action or run past the clip's end. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |

+| **Auto Zoom…** | | Zooms the selected screen recordings in at their clicks and typing and back out after, as ordinary actions, in one undo step, "Auto Zoom". See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/). | Every selected clip plays a movie that has a cursor file. It works inside a nest |

+| **Follow Subject…** | | Frames each selected movie clip on its subject, found on this Mac, with eased moves on its action lane and a blurred copy on a Backgrounds track where it shows the whole picture, in one undo step. See [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/). | A selected clip plays a movie. It works inside a nest |

+| **Add Shortcut Overlays** | | Shows each keyboard shortcut recorded in the selected screen recordings as keycaps at the moment it was pressed, on a "Shortcuts" track, in one undo step. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). | Every selected clip plays a movie that has a cursor file, and Frame Job isn't already reading the files. It works inside a nest |

+| **Speed Up Typing…** | | Plays the typing in the selected screen recordings faster where nobody speaks and no shortcut shows, in one undo step. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/). | Every selected clip plays a movie that has a cursor file. It works inside a nest |
+| **Speed…** | | Sets the selected clips' playback rate through a sheet, ×0.1 to ×1000. See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/). | The selection includes a clip that plays a media file |
+| **Speed Ramp…** | | Puts a speed ramp preset on one selected media clip. See [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it plays a media file |

+| **Retime Range…** | | Plays the in/out range faster or slower on every unlocked track and moves what follows to stay in step, in one undo step, "Retime Range". See [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). | An in/out range is set. It works inside a nest |
+  needs="Remove Filler Words… needs your AssemblyAI key, unless a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words."
+| Item | What it does | Available when |
+| **Remove Silences…** | Finds silent stretches and removes them, through a sheet. It needs no key. See [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/). | A clip plays sound |

+| **Remove Filler Words…** | Finds "um"s and "uh"s and removes them, through a sheet. See [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/). | A clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on, and either your AssemblyAI key is set or a file in scope has a transcript made with filler words |

+When the key is all that's missing, the item is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**, and its tooltip says where to set the key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
+**Transition ▸** sets the transition into the clip. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).

+The rows are **Cross Dissolve**, **Fade Through Black**, **Fade Through White**, **Push Left**, **Push Right**, **Push Up**, **Push Down**, **Wipe**, **Slide**, **Zoom**, **Wipe Left**, **Wipe Up** and **Wipe Down**, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's transition.
+| A transition | A selected clip has room for one, meaning an overlap or a hard cut. Other selected clips are skipped. |
+| **None** | Something is selected, so a stored transition the timeline doesn't draw can always be cleared. |
+At a hard cut it adds a transition 0.5 s long, snapped to frames. Where neither side of the cut has a frame to spare, a sheet says so and offers **Shift Clips Left**.
+**Motion ▸** sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves, and previews the result. Every item is available when a selected clip shows a picture. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
+| **In ▸** | **Fade**, **Zoom In**, **Zoom Out**, **Slide Left**, **Slide Right**, **Slide Up**, **Slide Down**, **Spin**, **Pop**, then **None** |
+| **Preview** | Sets the in/out range to the first selected clip with a picture, turns Loop on and plays it. The range and Loop stay set afterwards. |

+In each submenu a checkmark shows the kind every selected clip has. An In or Out kind with a length of zero reads "Fade (inactive)", or "Fade (some inactive)" when only some of the selected clips with that kind have zero length.
+Every During motion starts from where the clip is placed, so the clip's first frame sits exactly there.
+**Look ▸** puts a look or a LUT on the clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

+The rows are **Warm**, **Cool**, **Teal & Orange**, **Vivid**, **Faded**, **Vintage**, **Dramatic** and **Black & White**, then the project's `.cube` LUTs in Media list order when it has any, then **None**. The LUT rows are written each time the menu opens.
+A checkmark marks a look every selected clip has, and a dash marks one only some of them have. Each clip keeps its amount, and a clip with no look starts at full strength.
+It's available when a selected clip shows a picture from a file, or is an adjustment clip.
+**Remove Background** keeps the person and removes the rest of the picture, or turns that off. It has no key. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).

+It's checked when every selected clip has it, and shows a dash when some do. With every clip it can act on already cut out, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without, and each clip already cut out keeps its values.
+It's available when a selected clip plays a video file, is a freeze frame of one, or is a picture.

+**Camera Layout ▸** lays out the camera and the screen behind it at the playhead, eased over half a second and held until the next switch. One undo step, "Camera Layout". See [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/).
+| **Corner ▸** | The camera in a box in the corner you pick, with the screen at its full placement. The box is a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall and 5 % in from the edges. |
+| **Rounded Corner ▸** | The same with rounded corners. |
+| **Side by Side** | The screen fitted in the left two-thirds, and the camera cropped to fill the right third, with margins and a small radius. |
+| **Stacked** | The screen across the top, and the camera filling the rest below. |
+| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |
+| **Screen Only** | Hides the camera where it is. |
+**Corner ▸**, **Rounded Corner ▸** and **Circle ▸** each hold **Bottom Right**, **Bottom Left**, **Top Right** and **Top Left**.
+The camera's crop is centred on the person when the camera's masks are cached. A zoom in the way brings up a sheet offering **Nest and Switch**.

+It's available with two selected clips with a picture on different tracks, one selected clip with a picture, or, with nothing selected, a clip at the playhead on a track named "Camera". The camera has to contain the playhead. It works inside a nest.

+**Switch Angle ▸** re-picks the selected shot from another camera track that covers it, keeping its span, its switches and its dissolves, as one undo step. The new pieces are selected. See [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

+It has one row per track covering the shot's whole span, written each time the menu opens. There are up to nine, front first, named after their tracks, and tracks that share a name add their position, as in "Camera (2)". With no track to offer, the menu shows **No Covering Angle**, which is never available.
+A row is available when exactly one clip is selected, its track isn't locked, it isn't linked to a detached sound, and that row's track still covers it with video clips. It works inside a nest.
+Both commands put something on a new track behind everything. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
+| Item | What it does | Available when |
+| **Add Background ▸ Solid Color** | Adds a canvas-sized white plate the length of the timeline, selected so you can recolour it in the Clip tab's Fill row. There's no dialog. | Always |
+| **Add Background ▸ Image…** | Adds a picture you choose, at Fill scale, the length of the timeline. It takes images only. Importing and placing are one undo step. | Always |

+| **Add Blurred Background** | Adds a blurred copy of the picture at the same start, duration, speed and source window. The copy is muted, and has none of the clip's transition, actions or label. | Exactly one clip is selected and it has a picture size: a video, image, still, shape or graphic clip. Greyed for a nest, text, adjustment or audio-only clip |
+| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |

+| **Rename…** | <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> | Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline. It's also the way to rename a nest clip, because double-clicking one opens it. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/). | Something is selected |

+| **Label ▸** | | **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** and **Purple**, each with its colour dot, then **None**. A checkmark shows the label the selected clips share. One undo step, "Label Clip", and a colour every selected clip already carries beeps. | Something is selected |
+| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |

+| **Nest** | <kbd>⌘G</kbd> | Wraps the selected clips into one nest clip, which is selected afterwards. The nest's canvas is frozen at the project's current size. See [Nests](/editing/nests/). | Something is selected, other than a single nest clip on its own |
+| **Un-nest** | <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> | Breaks a nest clip back into its clips. The nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume are lost. | The selection includes a nest clip |
+| **Open Nest** | <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | Goes inside the selected nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it's a nest clip |
+| **Close Nest** | <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | Comes back out by one level. | A nest is open |
+**Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are greyed while you're typing in a text field.

lines: -  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its waveform and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."

+  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its fade handles and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."
Each clip draws as one block with 2 pt rounded corners and a thin border, so you can always see where one clip ends and the next begins.

-From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip and the waveform sit under a wash of the clip's own colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.

+From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip sits under a wash of the clip's own colour and the waveform is drawn on that colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.

The action lane shows a band for each [action](/motion/action-lane/). The selected action's span is also washed down the whole clip, in the action colour: mint in the dark look, a deeper green in the light one.

A clip with a name of its own shows that. Otherwise it shows what it holds: a nest's name, the file's name, the text itself, or the shape's kind. A clip with none of those reads as its kind, such as **Graphic** or **Adjustment**. A name too long for the strip ends in an ellipsis.
-On a narrow clip the strip gives things up from the right. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into it.
+On a narrow clip the strip leaves out what won't fit. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into the symbols.

- **A wedge** along the bottom of the name strip, from the left end for an In preset and from the right end for an Out preset. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and it rises towards its inner end, so you can see how far into the clip the motion runs. It's never shorter than 2 pt or wider than the clip.
- **A small wave** at the right end of the strip, to the left of any label dot, for a During movement.
-Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video, image or freeze frame clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.
+Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.

+A file's strip holds one frame for each second, so a thumbnail shows that point in the clip to within a second or so. It follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log file with a Camera Log set, or of a PQ or HLG file, shows the converted picture, not the flat image in the file.
+The strip covers the first 600 seconds of a file. Later in a longer file, the clip shows its plain colour.

-Each thumbnail is the source frame at that point in the clip, to the nearest earlier whole second of the source, and it follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log, PQ or HLG file shows the converted picture, not the flat image in the file.
+An image has one thumbnail, so only the first second of an image clip shows it. A freeze frame's strip starts at the moment it froze.
Text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no thumbnails.
-A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps.

+A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps. A nest clip draws no waveform, even when it has sound.

The waveform draws faded when the clip or its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track's mute button stays unlit under another track's solo, so the waveform is the place to look to see what's in the mix. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).

-A teal line across the picture part of a clip with [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) on shows where the clip fades out in each pause and back in before speech. The top is fully shown and the bottom is fully hidden.

content.text:
Node is updated: your default is now **22.23.4**, and `pnpm dev` works. The docs site is serving at http://localhost:4321 on the new version; I fetched the home page and a feature page and both came back fine. `node -v` should show v22.23.4; if a terminal you already had open doesn't, open a new one.

**I stopped a dev server I shouldn't have.** While testing, my command found a dev server already running on port 4321 (pid 6163), and my cleanup then stopped it. It was almost certainly yours, though its logs went with it, so I can't prove that. I started a replacement on the same port (pid 10171). If you ran yours in a terminal, that terminal will show it exited; to go back to your own, run `pnpm exec astro dev stop`, then `pnpm dev`.

## What was wrong
- **Cause:** mise manages your Node, and `~/.config/mise/config.toml` says `node = "22"`, meaning the newest 22.x installed. That was only 22.18.0, so your config didn't need changing.
- **My mistake:** the `.node-version` file I added never did anything, because your mise is set to ignore those files. I've corrected the docs that said it pinned the version, and it now names 22.23.4 for hosts and tools that do read it.

## What changed on your machine
- **Global tools:** these live inside each Node install, so a plain update would have dropped about 17 commands from your PATH, including `pnpm`, `gemini` and `tessl`. I copied them across at their exact versions.
- **Checks:** `pnpm`, `ncu`, `gemini`, `mmdc`, `drizzle-kit`, `devcontainer`, `license-checker` and `yo` all ran on the new Node. I didn't run `yarn`, `tessl` or `live-coding-music-mcp`, or your `npm link`ed tools; for those I only confirmed the links or commands resolve.
- **Every project:** any project using your global Node now gets 22.23.4.
- **Still on 22.18.0:** it's still installed, and your portive dev server keeps using it until you restart that server.

## One existing problem
`howdo` doesn't run as a command: `which howdo` finds nothing. Its `dist/index.js` has no execute permission, and that file is the same one the 22.18.0 install points to, so the update didn't cause this. To fix it, run `chmod +x ~/devel/howdo/cli-tool/dist/index.js`; I've left it for you.

## Docs site status
- **Writing:** it's still running, with 364 pages drafted and the fact-check and review passes still going, so pages will keep changing under your dev server.
- **`pnpm build`:** it currently fails on 3 broken links, which I expect from that unfinished work. `pnpm dev` doesn't run that check. I'll clear them in the final pass.

description: "a batch's leftovers (residue, review nits, small follow-ups) are done inside the current task when possible; file an issue only for what cannot be; never drop a task"
metadata:

---

When a batch turns up leftover work (residue, review nits, an unmeasured claim, a small follow-up), do it inside the current task if it can be done there. File a GitHub issue only for what cannot be done now (it needs the owner, it is large, it belongs to another area). Nothing that should be done is dropped silently.

**Why:** the owner said (2026-10-03) the open-issue count never fell because each batch filed new follow-ups instead of finishing them, and "we also need to finish this whole effort eventually". They corrected my reading of "don't file anything" as a blanket rule: "it's not 'stop filing', it's do tasks now if possible, otherwise file. """Site-wide deterministic scans: menu paths, keys and tool names against the source."""
import collections, glob, os, re, sys

REPO = '/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs'
sys.path.insert(0, f'{REPO}/tools/proof')
import docs_site_proof as proof

SITE = f'{REPO}/docs/site'
pages = proof.pages(SITE)
texts = {slug: open(path, encoding='utf-8').read() for slug, path in pages.items()}
menus = proof.menu_items()
tools, devs = proof.product_tools(), proof.dev_tools()
TOP = {'File', 'Edit', 'Insert', 'Clip', 'Track', 'Mark', 'View', 'Window', 'Help', 'Frame Job'}

# Menu titles built from enums and variables don't appear as literals, so read every string.
strings = set()
for path in glob.glob(f'{REPO}/app/Sources/*.swift'):
    strings |= set(re.findall(r'"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)+)"', open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()))

unknown = collections.Counter()
where = collections.defaultdict(set)
for slug, text in texts.items():
    found = re.findall(r'\*\*([^*\n]+?▸[^*\n]*?)\*\*', text)
    found += re.findall(r'''(?:menu=|['"])['"]?((?:File|Edit|Insert|Clip|Track|Mark|View|Window|Help|Frame Job) ▸ [^'"\n]+)['"]''', text)
    for path in found:
        parts = [p.strip() for p in path.split('▸') if p.strip()]
        if parts[0] not in TOP:
            continue
        for leaf in parts[1:]:
            leaf = re.sub(r'\s*\(.*$', '', leaf)
            if leaf in menus or leaf in strings or leaf + '…' in strings or leaf.rstrip('…') in strings:
                continue
            unknown[path] += 1
            where[path].add(slug)
print('== menu paths with a step found in no source string:', len(unknown))
for path, count in unknown.most_common(60):
    print(f'  {count:>3}  {path}   <- {sorted(where[path])[:2]}')

print('\n== tools named in AtAGlance that are not product tools')
for slug, text in texts.items():
    for block in re.findall(r'tools=(\{\[[^\]]*\]\}|"[^"]*")', text):
        for name in re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]+", block):
            if name not in tools:

const S = args.scratch
const R = args.repo

const SHELL = `Shell note: commands with heredocs, loops or variables can be refused here. Write any script to a file under ${S}/work/ with the Write tool, then run it as one plain command. - accepted: the writer rightly left something out (the code can't settle it, or it's unreachable, or third-party behaviour). Record it and change nothing.

${SHELL}

- summary: one plain sentence, under about 140 characters, saying what the reader gets. It must agree with the page. British spelling in prose, the app's spelling for its labels. - name: what a reader would call it. Rewrite names like "Note: nothing to analyse" or "detect_silence for agents" so they read as things a person looks for. In the mcp section, tool names stay as they are.
- where: a place a person can find it: a menu path, an inspector tab and section, or a gesture. No URLs, and no asides like "(after Close Gap, no shortcut)". Empty when there's nowhere to point. Menu paths must match the page.
- keys: the exact shortcut from the page, or absent.
- needs: only a key or permission the feature truly requires, or absent.
- anchor: leave it alone.
If a row describes something the page says doesn't exist or doesn't work, or that a person can't reach, remove it. If two rows in your section are the same thing, remove one.

Write ${S}/inventory/feature-fixes/${section}.json:
{"updates":[{"id":"<row id>","name":"…","summary":"…","where":"…","keys":"…","needs":"…"}],"remove":[{"id":"<row id>","reason":"…"}]}
Include only the fields you are changing, and use an empty string to clear one. Validate it with python3 -m json.tool. Do not edit features.json or any page.

${SHELL}

Return the file, the number of rows you read, how many you updated and removed, and any page you suspect is wrong.`, { label: 'rows:' + section, phase: 'Reconcile', schema: ROWS, effort: 'medium' })

const AGREE = { type: 'object', properties: { facts_compared: { type: 'number' }, fixes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { pages: { type: 'string' }, was: { type: 'string' }, now: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['pages', 'was', 'now'] } }, app_defects: { type: 'array', items: DEFECT } }, required: ['facts_compared', 'fixes', 'app_defects'] }

const PAIRS = [
  ['audio', 'audio/*, and mcp/tools-set-audio, mcp/tools-audio'],
  ['color-hdr', 'color/*, hdr/*, and mcp/tools-set-video'],
  ['motion-speed', 'motion/*, speed/*, and mcp/tools-animation, mcp/tools-speed, mcp/tools-transitions'],
  ['edit-timeline', 'editing/*, timeline/*, and mcp/tools-move-and-trim, mcp/tools-cut-and-delete, mcp/tools-copy-and-nest, mcp/tools-adding-clips, mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers, reference/gestures, reference/keyboard-shortcuts, reference/menus, reference/clip-menu'],
  ['canvas-effects', 'canvas/*, text-and-shapes/*, effects/*, and mcp/tools-set-video, mcp/tools-clip-properties, reference/context-menus'],
  ['captions-cleanup', 'captions/*, cleanup/*, and mcp/tools-captions, mcp/tools-clean-up, mcp/tools-analysis'],
  ['framing-multicam', 'framing/*, multicam/*, and mcp/tools-framing, mcp/tools-multicam'],
  ['graphics', 'graphics/*, and mcp/tools-graphics, mcp/tools-graphic-files'],
  ['recording', 'recording/*, and mcp/record-screen, mcp/tools-recording'],
  ['export', 'export/*, and mcp/export, mcp/render-frame, mcp/tools-render-and-export, reference/file-formats, reference/limits'],
  ['basics', 'getting-started/*, projects/*, assistant/*, and reference/settings, reference/remembered-choices, reference/file-locations, reference/framejob-package, reference/troubleshooting, reference/glossary, mcp/tools-projects, mcp/tools-media'],
]

const agree = ([name, pages]) => agent(`You are checking that the public documentation for Frame Job, a native macOS video editor, agrees with itself, in docs/site/ of ${R} (your working directory). ${RULES}

The pages were written and fact-checked one small chunk at a time, so no checker saw two sections. The same fact is often stated in several places: a person-facing page, the MCP tool page that does the same thing, and a reference page. Your scope: ${pages} (under ${C}).

Read all of them. Find every fact stated in more than one place: a default, a range, a unit, a limit, an option list, a name, a shortcut, when something is available, what it does. Where two statements disagree, or one is broader than the other in a way that misleads, read the code to find which is right, and fix the wrong one in place. Don't restyle anything else.

Also check:
- Sibling pages don't contradict each other, and a concept is called the same thing across them.
- Each "With an agent" section points at the right tool, and links to it where one exists. A tool's heading anchor is its name, for example /mcp/tools-speed/#set_speed.
- Terms: one word for one thing, and the glossary's word where it has one.

A decision already made: real arrow keys don't nudge clips on the canvas, and Copy, Cut and Paste don't work on a nest clip, so don't restore any claim that they do. Another agent is removing those claims.

If the code shows the app itself is wrong (a control that can't work, two descriptions of one thing in the app that disagree), don't paper over it: report it with file:line and a severity (data-loss, broken, minor, cosmetic).

${CHECKS}

${SHELL}

Return how many shared facts you compared, each fix with its evidence, and any app defects.`, { label: 'agree:' + name, phase: 'Reconcile', schema: AGREE, effort: 'high' })

const READER = { type: 'object', properties: { questions: { type: 'number' }, answered_well: { type: 'number' }, fixed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { question: { type: 'string' }, change: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['question', 'change'] } }, unanswerable: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, app_defects: { type: 'array', items: DEFECT } }, required: ['questions', 'answered_well', 'fixed', 'unanswerable', 'app_defects'] }

const PEOPLE = [
  ['creator', 'a creator who records screen tutorials and talking-head videos and posts them to YouTube and TikTok, new to Frame Job, coming from CapCut or ScreenFlow'],
  ['podcaster', 'a podcast editor with two guests, two cameras and separate microphones, coming from Premiere or Descript, who cares about sound, sync and turning the show into vertical clips'],
  ['finisher', 'an experienced colourist and finishing editor coming from DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut, who shoots log and delivers HDR and ProRes masters and wants exact behaviour'],
  ['agent-builder', 'a developer who wants an AI agent to drive Frame Job over MCP and who also wants to write custom motion graphics, reading the docs to get a first session working'],
]

const reader = ([name, who]) => agent(`You are testing the public documentation for Frame Job, a native macOS video editor, as a real reader. The site is docs/site/ in ${R} (your working directory). ${RULES}

You are ${who}. First write down 30 specific questions this person would really ask: how do I…, can it…, why won't it…, what's the difference between…, what happens to my… when…. Think of their first hour, then their first real project, and the moment something goes wrong. Write the questions before you look at the site.

Then, for each question, look for the answer as they would: the sidebar's section and page titles in docs/site/sidebar.mjs and each page's title, then a word search with grep over ${C} as the site's search box would, using their words, not the app's. A competitor's term is a fair search.

Score each one. An answer is good only if the page that a reader would land on says it plainly.

Fix what fails them, checking the code before you add any fact:
- The answer exists but is hard to find: add a cross-link, or the reader's word to a description or a sentence, so that search finds it.
- The answer is missing: add it to the right page.
- The answer misleads: correct it.
Don't add pages. If a question can't be answered because the app can't do it, a short honest note on the nearest page is worth more than silence, if the reader would otherwise keep looking. Don't name competitors' products on a page.

A decision already made: real arrow keys don't nudge clips on the canvas, and Copy, Cut and Paste don't work on a nest clip.

${CHECKS}

${SHELL}

Return the number of questions, how many were already answered well, what you changed, what stays unanswerable and why, and any app defect you found.`, { label: 'reader:' + name, phase: 'Readers', schema: READER, effort: 'high' })

phase('Reconcile')
const first = await parallel([
  () => leftovers().then((r) => ({ leftovers: r })),
  ...PAIRS.map((pair) => () => agree(pair).then((r) => ({ agree: { name: pair[0], ...r } }))),
  ...args.sections.map((section) => () => rows(section).then((r) => ({ rows: { section, ...r } }))),
])
const got = first.filter(Boolean)
log(`Reconcile: ${got.length} of ${1 + PAIRS.length + args.sections.length} agents`)

phase('Readers')
const readers = (await parallel(PEOPLE.map((person) => () => reader(person).then((r) => r && { name: person[0], ...r })))).filter(Boolean)

const rowsDone = got.map((r) => r.rows).filter(Boolean)
const agreeDone = got.map((r) => r.agree).filter(Boolean)
const left = got.map((r) => r.leftovers).filter(Boolean)[0]
return {
  leftovers: left,
  agree_fixes: agreeDone.flatMap((a) => a.fixes.map((f) => ({ area: a.name, ...f }))),
  facts_compared: agreeDone.reduce((n, a) => n + a.facts_compared, 0),
  rows: rowsDone.map((r) => ({ section: r.section, rows: r.rows, updated: r.updated, removed: r.removed, contradictions: r.contradictions })),
  readers: readers.map((r) => ({ name: r.name, questions: r.questions, answered_well: r.answered_well, fixed: r.fixed.length, unanswerable: r.unanswerable })),
  reader_fixes: readers.flatMap((r) => r.fixed.map((f) => ({ reader: r.name, ...f }))),
  app_defects: [...(left?.app_defects ?? []), ...agreeDone.flatMap((a) => a.app_defects), ...readers.flatMap((r) => r.app_defects)],
}

  () => leftovers().then((r) => ({ leftovers: r })),
  ...PAIRS.map((pair) => () => agree(pair).then((r) => ({ agree: { name: pair[0], ...r } }))),
  ...args.sections.map((section) => () => rows(section).then((r) => ({ rows: { section, ...r } }))),
])
const got = first.filter(Boolean)
log(`Reconcile: ${got.length} of ${1 + PAIRS.length + args.sections.length} agents`)

phase('Readers')
const readers = (await parallel(PEOPLE.map((person) => () => reader(person).then((r) => r && { name: person[0], ...r })))).filter(Boolean)

const rowsDone = got.map((r) => r.rows).filter(Boolean)
const agreeDone = got.map((r) => r.agree).filter(Boolean)
const left = got.map((r) => r.leftovers).filter(Boolean)[0]
return {
  leftovers: left,
  agree_fixes: agreeDone.flatMap((a) => a.fixes.map((f) => ({ area: a.name, ...f }))),
  facts_compared: agreeDone.reduce((n, a) => n + a.facts_compared, 0),
  rows: rowsDone.map((r) => ({ section: r.section, rows: r.rows, updated: r.updated, removed: r.removed, contradictions: r.contradictions })),
  readers: readers.map((r) => ({ name: r.name, questions: r.questions, answered_well: r.answered_well, fixed: r.fixed.length, unanswerable: r.unanswerable })),
  reader_fixes: readers.flatMap((r) => r.fixed.map((f) => ({ reader: r.name, ...f }))),
  app_defects: [...(left?.app_defects ?? []), ...agreeDone.flatMap((a) => a.app_defects), ...readers.flatMap((r) => r.app_defects)],
}

Return your verdict.`, { label: 'verify:' + defect.id, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT, effort: 'high' })

log(`confirmed ${by('confirmed').length}, refuted ${by('refuted').length}, deliberate ${by('deliberate').length}, already filed ${by('already-filed').length}`)
return { distinct: list.defects.length, verdicts }

"""Make the feature list's `where` and `keys` read one way, whichever section wrote them."""
import collections, json, re

PATH = '/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/src/data/features.json'
data = json.load(open(PATH))


def where(text):
    text = re.sub(r'^Inspector ▸ Clip tab ▸ ', 'Clip tab ▸ ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'^Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ ', 'Clip tab ▸ ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'^Inspector ▸ (Media|Document|Transcript|Assistant)(?: tab)? ▸ ', r'\1 tab ▸ ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'^Inspector ▸ (Media|Document|Transcript|Assistant)(?: tab)?$', r'\1 tab', text)
    text = re.sub(r'^(Clip tab ▸ (?:Picture|Color|Sound|Clip)) sub-tab', r'\1', text)
    return text


def keys(text):
    # One separator, ' or ', which the page splits on. A comma alone can be the key itself.
    text = text.replace(' / ', ' or ')
    return re.sub(r'(?<=\S\S), (?=\S\S)', ' or ', text)


changed = collections.Counter()
prefixes = collections.Counter()
for section in data['sections']:
    for row in section['features']:
        if row.get('where') in ('Automatic', 'automatic'):
            del row['where']
            changed['automatic'] += 1
        if 'where' in row:
            new = where(row['where'])
            changed['where'] += new != row['where']
            row['where'] = new
            prefixes[new.split(' ▸ ')[0]] += 1
        if 'keys' in row:
            new = keys(row['keys'])
            changed['keys'] += new != row['keys']
            row['keys'] = new
json.dump(data, open(PATH, 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print(dict(changed))
print(prefixes.most_common(16))

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'framejob-verify-defects',
  description: 'Dedupe the app defects found while documenting Frame Job, then try to refute each one, and confirm the docs describe the real behaviour',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Dedupe', detail: 'merge reports of one root cause' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per defect, default refuted; aligns the docs with what the app does' },
  ],
}

const S = args.scratch
const R = args.repo
const ISSUES = args.issues

phase('Dedupe')
const LIST = { type: 'object', properties: { file: { type: 'string' }, defects: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, title: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'title'] } } }, required: ['file', 'defects'] }
const list = await agent(`${S}/defects-raw.json has 107 reports of possible defects in Frame Job, a native macOS video editor, found by agents reading the code while writing its documentation. The repo is ${R} (your working directory, read-only). Many are the same defect reported several times.

Group the reports by root cause, reading the code only as far as you need to tell two reports apart. Write ${S}/defects.json: {"defects":[{"id":"d01","title":"…","severity":"data-loss|broken|minor|cosmetic","evidence":"the best evidence, with file:line","raw":[indices into the raw list]}]}.

Keep user-visible behaviour separate from text. Put reports that concern ONLY source comments into one entry, id "comments", with all of them in its evidence. Put reports that concern only an agent tool's description text into one entry, id "tool-text". Text a person sees in the app that is wrong stays its own entry. Order by severity. Every raw report must land in exactly one entry. Validate with python3 -m json.tool.

Shell note: heredocs and loops can be refused here, so write any script to a file under ${S}/work/ and run it plainly. Do not run git.

Return the file and the list of ids and titles.`, { label: 'dedupe', phase: 'Dedupe', schema: LIST, effort: 'high' })

log(`Dedupe: ${list.defects.length} distinct defects`)

phase('Verify')
const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    id: { type: 'string' },
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'refuted', 'deliberate', 'already-filed'] },
    issue: { type: 'string', description: 'the existing issue number, when already filed' },
    severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['data-loss', 'broken', 'minor', 'cosmetic'] },
    title: { type: 'string', description: 'an issue title: what the person sees, not the cause' },
    reproduce: { type: 'string', description: 'steps a person can follow, or how it was shown' },
    cause: { type: 'string', description: 'the root cause with file:line' },
    fix: { type: 'string', description: 'the smallest likely fix' },
    how_known: { type: 'string', description: 'read from the code, or run, and what was run' },
    reasoning: { type: 'string', description: 'why this verdict, especially what was tried in order to refute it' },
    docs_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['id', 'verdict', 'severity', 'title', 'reasoning', 'how_known'],
}

const verify = (defect) => agent(`You are a skeptic. An agent reading the code of Frame Job, a native macOS video editor, reported the defect below. Your job is to try to REFUTE it. The repo is ${R} (your working directory). If you can't show it's real, the verdict is refuted.

Defect ${defect.id}: ${defect.title}
Full report: the entry with id "${defect.id}" in ${S}/defects.json. The original reports are in ${S}/defects-raw.json.

Do this:
1. Read the code path end to end, from the user's action to what they see, including every caller, and look for what the report missed: a guard elsewhere, a second path that handles the case, a flag that's set differently than assumed.
2. Check whether it's deliberate. Search designs/spec/11-decisions/ (start at its README.md), designs/adr/ and docs/manual-checks.md. An accepted limit recorded there is verdict "deliberate".
3. Check whether it's already known. ${ISSUES} lists every open issue. Run gh issue list --search "<words>" --state all for closed ones if the title suggests it. A match is verdict "already-filed", with the number.
4. If you can settle it cheaply by running something small, do: a Swift or Python script under ${S}/work/ that exercises the same API or logic. Say exactly what you ran. Do not launch Frame Job, and do not touch the clipboard.
5. If it's real, say what a person sees, write steps they could follow, give the root cause as file:line and the smallest likely fix. Rate severity honestly: data-loss only if work can really be lost past Undo, broken if a feature doesn't do what it's for, minor if it's an edge case or wrong message, cosmetic otherwise.

Then check the docs. Whatever your verdict, the site (docs/site/src/content/docs/) and the guide (docs/guide/) must describe what the app does TODAY. Grep both for the behaviour. If a page promises what the app doesn't do, correct it to the real behaviour, in plain words with no mention of bugs or issues: a page says what happens, not why it's wrong. Read ${R}/docs/site/CLAUDE.md before you edit a site page, and check it with:
  node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs docs/site/src/content/docs/<slug>.mdx
  python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages docs/site/src/content/docs/<slug>.mdx
Change no app code. Don't rename headings.

For the "comments" and "tool-text" entries: verify each item in the entry. "tool-text" means an agent tool's description in app/Sources/AgentCatalog*.swift is wrong. Return one verdict for the entry, and list the real items in reproduce.

Shell note: heredocs and loops can be refused here, so write any script to a file under ${S}/work/ with the Write tool and run it plainly. Do not run git. Other agents are editing nearby pages, so make small edits and re-read a file just before editing it.

Return your verdict.`, { label: 'verify:' + defect.id, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT, effort: 'high' })

const verdicts = (await parallel(list.defects.map((d) => () => verify(d)))).filter(Boolean)
const by = (v) => verdicts.filter((x) => x.verdict === v)
log(`confirmed ${by('confirmed').length}, refuted ${by('refuted').length}, deliberate ${by('deliberate').length}, already filed ${by('already-filed').length}`)
return { distinct: list.defects.length, verdicts }

effects :: Minor page wording, not edited: remove-background.mdx's Good to know says a clip draws whole only when no frame 'has a person', which does not cover a picture with Subject set to Foreground (No subject found, covered elsewhere on the page). 

effects :: Cleared keys: the Esc cancel key on chroma-key-pick-from-canvas and obscure-place-on-canvas, and the bare ⌥ modifier on obscure-canvas-grips, now in that row's summary. None of the three is a shortcut for the feature. 

effects :: Left the where prefix 'Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Picture ▸ …' as is, because 478 rows across the file use it, although the pages' AtAGlance says 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ …'. Normalising it is a whole-file choice. 

motion :: motion/edit-an-action (omission, not an error): 'Edit on the canvas' doesn't list the arrow-key nudge, but PreviewCanvasView.nudge writes through editTarget, so a nudge does change the selected action's end state. The code wins, so I kept 'nudging' in the canvas-edits-action-end row. The page could add it. 

speed :: speed/rate-stretch.mdx, Snapping: says 'Hold ⌘ as you press to turn snapping off for that drag'. TimelineView.continueGesture rebuilds the snapper from the current flags on every drag tick, so ⌘ works at any time during the drag and releasing it snaps again, as timeline/snapping.mdx says. I kept the row's keys '⌘ while dragging' because the code supports them; the page needs fixing. 

speed :: speed/edit-a-ramped-clip.mdx, 'An action past the clip's end': says an action partly or wholly past the end can still have its curve changed, be moved earlier or be shortened. speed/sound-at-high-speed.mdx says an action wholly past the end has no band you can reach. The code agrees with that: ActionLaneView.bandRects places such a band beyond the lane, and syncSelectedAction can't reach it with the playhead. I found no way for a person to select it short of lengthening the clip, though I didn't trace every selection path. The row now says 'while its band shows'; the page may need the same limit, or a note that this is agent-only. 

export :: Checked against the code and found consistent: encoder memory figures in export/encoder-speed.mdx (AV1 MP4) and export/export-queue.mdx (MP4 and WebM ranges) match ExportEncoderCosts.swift, so their different ranges are not an error. 'Measuring loudness…' on every export with sound matches Exporter.swift. The APNG save panel message matches the format string in ExportSheetCommit.swift, assuming the container value is 'apng', which I did not read. Quit Frame Job with ⌘Q matches AppDelegate+Menus.swift. 

export :: export-queue-quit-guard keeps keys ⌘Q even though export/export-queue.mdx never shows that shortcut; it comes from reference/menus.mdx and the code. export-presets-file keeps its ~/Library path as where, because the page gives that location, although it is not a menu path.

Quitting while the Exporting sheet is writing doesn't ask, and can leave the partly written file behind. Cancel the export first.

Only the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) is guarded at quit, so jobs there ask before they stop.

===== d05 broken Option-dragging a clip with another clip right after it moves the clip instead of copying it
-- reproduce: 1. Put two clips back to back on one track, for example by splitting a clip with ⌘T.
2. Hold ⌥, press on the first clip, and drag it to an empty track or empty time.
3. Release. The clip has moved and a gap is left behind. No copy exists, nothing beeps, and no reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Edit ▸ Undo reads "Undo Move Clips", not "Undo Duplicate Clips".

For comparison, ⌘D on the same clip beeps and shows the overlap reason. ⌥-drag on the last clip of the run copies normally.

When that interim spot is refused, `copies` stays empty and the session silently becomes a plain move (app/Sources/TimelineSessions.swift:176-190).
