Related: [[litecode-stacked-phases]], [[implement-means-run-all-phases]], [[shared-working-tree-staging]], [[residue-do-now-else-file]].
---
name: implement-means-run-all-phases
description: "when the user says to implement a road map (e.g. via litecode), run every phase back to back and commit each; do not stop to ask between phases"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 03e5a54e-1d53-41ac-a701-66dfef5dc27f
  modified: 2026-10-01T18:51:34.832Z
---

When the user asks for a road map to be implemented ("begin with /litecode", "implement this"), carry it through every phase in order — one litecode pipeline per phase, commit each phase when its pipeline passes, then start the next — without pausing to ask "shall I continue?" between phases. Stop only for a real STOP (a stage's `STOP:`, a decision that is the user's, a spend, a failing verification that can't be resolved).

**Why:** on 2026-10-01, after road map 14's MC0 passed, I asked whether to commit and start MC1; the user replied "I'm confused. I want you to implement this. It's not a handoff."

**How to apply:** litecode's per-run "Finish" summary is a checkpoint, not a hand-back; print it, commit, and dispatch the next phase's triage. Related: [[roadmap-phases-via-subagents]], [[litecode-stacked-phases]].
---
name: residue-do-now-else-file
description: "a batch's leftovers (residue, review nits, small follow-ups) are done inside the current task when possible; file an issue only for what cannot be; never drop a task"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a batch turns up leftover work (residue, review nits, an unmeasured claim, a small follow-up), do it inside the current task if it can be done there. File a GitHub issue only for what cannot be done now (it needs the owner, it is large, it belongs to another area). Nothing that should be done is dropped silently.

**Why:** the owner said (2026-10-03) the open-issue count never fell because each batch filed new follow-ups instead of finishing them, and "we also need to finish this whole effort eventually". They corrected my reading of "don't file anything" as a blanket rule: "it's not 'stop filing', it's do tasks now if possible, otherwise file. Ultimately I don't want to lose tasks that should be done."

**How to apply:** in [[issue-batching-workflow]] batches, tell the designer and implementer to fold small residue into the batch (BATCH-RULES.md says so since 2026-10-03). At the finish step, go through the implementer's Residue and the reviewer's nits: fix or measure each now, record a genuinely accepted limit in spec §11, and file only the remainder. Something the owner explicitly waved off (e.g. the double ffmpeg question, 2026-10-03) is neither done nor filed.
---
name: litecode-stacked-phases
description: How to run many /litecode pipelines back to back in Reelcut when the user commits only on request - tree-object baselines, reader reviews mapped onto litecode's cast, residue pipelines, rule H
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-19/20 the user asked for four road-map items "using /litecode for
each phase" and ten pipelines ran back to back with NO commits between
them, because the user commits only when they ask. What made that work:

- **A baseline per pipeline.** Before each run, write the working tree to a
  git TREE object with a temporary index (`cp .git/index tmp;
  GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git add -A; GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git write-tree`) and put
  the hash in `request.md`. The run's diff is `git diff <tree>`. Untracked
  files show there as wholly deleted, which is noise: say so in the request,
  and give `git show <tree>:<path> | diff - <path>` for them.
- **A reader review fits litecode's fixed cast**: the designer writes the
  review PLAN (diffs, the questions verbatim, what is already known with
  citations, named mutants of TODAY's tree, never an old binary, which aborts
  the instruments), the implementer is the readers one question at a time and
  fixes survivors, the reviewer is the SCEPTIC told to refute findings and
  break fixes. Record the deviation (sequential readers, one sceptic).
- **litecode never runs a second fix pass.** When the second review still
  says fix-required, run a small RESIDUE pipeline for code or proof changes,
  and close prose nits by hand. Either way nothing stays only in the handoff
  directory: see [[write-findings-into-repo-documents]].
- **Rule H**: any command that could loop without bound (a reverted-fix test,
  a mutant, a stress call) runs under a hard wall-clock limit, kills only the
  process group it started, and records an expiry as the row's answer.
- **The sceptics' verdicts were mostly about the RECORD**: a sentence that
  claimed more than a run printed, a count that did not match its own list, a
  true threshold with a false explanation. Tell every stage: a number is
  written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a CONTROL.
- **A reader's fix is where the worst defect hid**: swapping a snapping
  argument reader for a plain one removed the only ceiling and `Int64.max`
  crashed the app. A fix that changes how an argument is read keeps its
  bounds and is tried at the extremes.

- **A big feature splits into pipelines by what can be PROVED alone**
  (C1, 2026-09-20/21: tolls, pure parts with a probe, the run with its MCP
  proof, the chrome, then live rows and the closing record, then the reader
  review). Draft the next pipeline's `request.md` while the current one
  runs, and finalise it with a "what the last pipeline found that binds you"
  section and the new baseline tree.
- **Subagents will not edit a `CLAUDE.md`, and should not.** A map entry or
  a rule clause a phase makes false is the orchestrator's to apply by hand,
  after the pipeline's last review, recorded in the tree and told to the
  user.
- **When a command is denied, stop that action** — report what is left
  (paths, the one command) and carry on with the rest; never route the same
  deletion through another tool.

**Why:** the user wants every item finished and everything findable, and is
not at the machine to answer between pipelines.
**How to apply:** reuse this shape for any multi-phase request; pass each
pipeline's lessons forward in the next `request.md`. See also
[[roadmap-phases-via-subagents]] and [[user-prefers-my-recommendation]].

## Where to work (binding for every stage)

- Work ONLY in the git worktree **{WT}** (branch `{BR}`), never in /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob (the integration checkout) and never in another lane's worktree (~/devel/framejob-lane-a, -b, -c run at the same time). Use absolute paths under the worktree for every read, edit and command (`cd {WT} && ...`). The worktree's CLAUDE.md, app/CLAUDE.md, core/CLAUDE.md and mcp-proxy/CLAUDE.md are the rulebook.
- The baseline is the worktree's HEAD: the run's diff is `git -C {WT} diff HEAD` plus `git -C {WT} status --porcelain` for new files.
- The issue text is the brief: `gh issue view <N> --comments` (run it from the worktree). Its numbers come from earlier measurements; re-measure before you build on one, and if a claim is false against the code, say so.
- Do NOT commit, push, or edit any CLAUDE.md. List any CLAUDE.md edit the change makes necessary under "CLAUDE.md edits owed" in your notes; the integrator applies them.
- A decision the owner has already made in spec §11 is not re-litigated (designs/spec/11-decisions/). A change that needs a NEW decision records it in §11 before the code. If the fix needs a genuine owner choice (a trade-off between behaviours, a cost, dropping something they asked for), write `STOP: <the question, with the options and your recommendation>` at the top of your output instead of choosing.
- Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`. Never spend money (no `--live` proofs).
- Verification follows CLAUDE.md "Verification": targeted tests/probes in the loop; `make typecheck` after Swift edits; `make lint` after Rust edits; `make app-debug` before driving the app over MCP (launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` and stop only that pid); mutants for the decisions the change adds; then `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground. The proof recorded for the change also runs once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`). Record each command and its result; a number in a record is written only when a run printed it.
- A user-visible behaviour change updates its page in docs/guide/ (and its README highlight or menus-and-shortcuts.md row if it adds one), spec §5.2/§6/§7.9 for anything they mirror, and every user-visible edit has its MCP mirror. A check only a person can make is a row in docs/manual-checks.md in the same change.
- File size rules: a file at ~600 lines gives something up (a pure move) before it takes anything on; new files ≤ 400; frozen files (EditorViewController.swift, TimelineView.swift, PreviewCanvasView.swift, AgentServer.swift) take wiring only. Ledger: `wc -l app/Sources/*.swift core/src/*.rs graphic/src/*.rs | sort -rn`.
- Never run `xcodegen` bare; use `make project`.
- Residue rule: a problem the batch uncovers in code it is in is fixed in this batch; only work that needs the owner or is as big as the batch itself is left, and it goes in the notes under "To file" with a draft title and body.
- The machine is shared with two other lanes: builds are slower, and wall-clock or audio-timing measurements can be noisy. Where a measurement is timing-sensitive, repeat it and say how many runs it took.

- `reading` alone is never a confirmation, except for a source comment or a text string.

- **Never edit any CLAUDE.md.** List each edit needed under "CLAUDE.md edits owed", with the exact text. The integrator applies them. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` included.

### Verification

Follows the root CLAUDE.md's "Verification" section.

- Run targeted tests and probes in the loop. `make typecheck` after Swift edits: 0 errors and exactly the 4 baseline warnings. `make lint` after Rust edits.
- `make app-debug` before driving the app. Launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch`, and stop only that pid.
- Run mutants for the decisions the batch adds.
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Run the batch's proof once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a control.
- Timing is noisy with three lanes running. Repeat a timing-sensitive measurement and say how many runs it took.

### Commits

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (I's HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit on I. A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

### Things never to do

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call. The assistant is driven only against its stand-in server.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard: it overwrites the owner's clipboard. Use a probe that keeps to a private pasteboard, or say `cannot-run`.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.
- **Kill only a pid you launched.** The owner's `/Applications/Frame Job.app` is running and is left alone. So is the docs dev server on port 4321.
- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

]

The fix round is running in three lanes in the background, covering all 58 issues in 12 batches. Nothing has been confirmed or fixed yet.

**Confirming first:** each batch starts by running its bugs in the real app with a test project, and the design work only starts after that.
- **Base build:** all three lanes run a frozen build of the code as it stood when the bugs were filed, so one lane's fix can't hide another lane's bug. Each fix also needs a test that fails on that build and passes on the fix.
- **Bugs that don't reproduce:** they aren't fixed. If an app run of the issue's steps shows correct behaviour, the issue is closed as not planned with what was run, and any docs page that states the bug is corrected.
- **`unverified` label:** it only comes off after a run in the built app.
- **Key and gesture bugs:** the app can't be sent real key presses or drags by script. Those bugs run through the app's own code in a test build, and the issue says so. They keep the label, and what only a person can check goes on your manual checks list.

**Docs commit:** you didn't say whether the docs work should go to `main`, but the lanes need it. I committed it as `f3697497` on `worktree-help-docs` and integrate every fix there. `main` is still at `b4b22392` and nothing is pushed, so moving this to `main` is your call.

content.content:
475 Should crop mode stay open to text, shape and graphic clips on a matte track? MT-4 has crop shape the matte, and these kinds have no Crop section, so C and the double-click are a person's only way to crop one. Options: A, keep it (this batch's interim, today's behaviour; such a crop still has no field and no Reset there). B, refuse there too (one rule on every track, only set_video crops these kinds; corrects matte-tracks.mdx line 83 and canvas-and-layers.md 789-791, and removes primaryRefusesCrop's track condition, row S12 and mutant matte-gate-off). C, give these kinds a Crop section on a matte track (a new section that amends spec 04.3b). Recommendation: A, because a matte is the one place spec 11 names a crop on these kinds and A takes nothing away. #475 is fixed everywhere else; whether it closes waits on this answer.

497 Should a folder dropped on the Media tab import what is in it? A: import its visible files one level down, leaving out hidden files and packages, skipping non-media without an alert, with import_media on a folder mirroring it. B: refuse at the drag, with no copy badge, and leave a folder in a mixed drop out without a word. C: keep the drop with its own sentence, "<name> is a folder. Open it and drop the files inside." Recommendation: A, since a shoot folder is what people drag and the current alert reads as a fault.

## Held for the owner
**#469, its second paragraph: a drag past a finished action that is not a first-frame cut** (a zoom, a mid-clip layout switch). Today it writes the base, so the picture stays put and frames before the action shift, with an undo step. CI-2 ("The playhead no longer decides where an edit lands") and CI-13 make that the rule, so changing it is a trade-off between two behaviours. This batch leaves it, pins it with D7 and D11, and leaves those page sentences alone. #469 stays open for this.
- **A: keep it.** CI-2 and CI-13 stand and the docs' "Select the action first" stays. A drag, a nudge and a typed value keep writing one place.
- **B: the drag lands where it shows.** With no action selected, a gesture goes to the latest finished action holding a key it writes. Amends CI-2 and CI-13. The playhead then picks where a canvas edit lands, frames before the action stay put, and a typed X at the same playhead still writes the base unless the inspector follows.
- **C: keep the base write but say why.** No undo step, and the canvas refuses with a sentence naming the action that holds the key. The issue's own fallback.

Recommendation: B, with the inspector's fields decided in the same answer. A drag that moves nothing and adds an undo step is the worse surprise.

The skill is the orchestrator's playbook, and the implementer is its stage 3; an implementer calling it would start a whole second pipeline inside that stage. The lane script plays the orchestrator instead. It follows the skill's rules: small or full route, review skipped only for a diff under 80 lines with every check passing, at most 5 fix passes, and a stop when a review repeats a finding.

The runs depart from the skill as written in four places:

- **A confirm stage before triage**, for your "confirm the bug actually exists first". It's run by litecode's designer agent, before any design.
- **Three pipelines at once**, for your lanes request. The skill says one agent at a time; each lane is still strictly one agent at a time.
- **An integrator after the review.** It commits, runs `make gate`, and comments on and closes the issues. The skill leaves committing to the orchestrator.
- **Two tiny helper agents:** one copies the spec when the adversary has no objections (the skill has the orchestrator do it), and in round 3 one waits for a3 to land.

So the next run needs no change. The only way to use the skill more literally is for me to run `/litecode` once per batch in this conversation, which means one batch at a time and no lanes. I'd keep the lanes.

"""Print every review's nits and non-blocking findings, from each batch's last review file."""
import glob
import os
import re

ROOT = '/Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/'
for d in sorted(glob.glob(ROOT + 'db-*')):
    reviews = sorted(glob.glob(d + '/07-review-*.md')) or glob.glob(d + '/05-review.md')
    if not reviews:
        continue
    text = open(reviews[-1]).read()
    out, keep = [], False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^#+ ', line):
            keep = bool(re.search(r'nit|minor|suggest|optional|follow|non-block|observ', line, re.I))
            if keep:
                out.append(line)
            continue
        if keep and line.strip():
            out.append(line[:300])
    print('===', os.path.basename(d), os.path.basename(reviews[-1]))
    print('\n'.join(out[:16]) if out else '  (no nit section)')

The docs-bug work is finished. All 58 issues (#461–#518) are closed, and the fixes plus the review leftovers are committed on `worktree-help-docs`. `main` is still at `b4b22392` and nothing is pushed.

**What was found:** every issue went through the confirm step before anything was designed, and every one reproduced. None turned out to be wrong. Several were narrower than filed: Loop failing only some of the time, for example, and Danish and German subtitle files not failing the way the issue said.

**What was done:**
- 55 issues were fixed. The other 3 were settled by your answers: #475 keeps crop mode on matte tracks, #497 imports a dropped folder's files, and #469 refuses a drag and names the action to select. #497 and #469 needed code; #475 needed only the decision written down.
- Every fix has a test that fails on the code as it was when the bugs were filed and passes on the fix. The changes also got targeted mutation tests to show those tests can fail.
- Every batch passed `make gate`. The final docs-site build has 366 pages, and every internal link is valid.
- A last round fixed the reviewers' nits instead of filing them. Only the last item turned up no bug; it added proof rows.

**What's still open:**
- **`unverified`:** 23 issues keep the label. They were confirmed and fixed by running the app's own code in a test build (keys, drags, the clipboard, the quit path), or for one string, by reading it in the built app. The real key presses and drags are rows on your manual checks list.
- **Follow-ups:** 16 issues were filed, #519–#534, plus one on the shared assistant helper in `doctored-dev` (rasterize's new name on GitHub). Two worth knowing about:
  - #531: cancelling an export while it's writing over an existing file still loses that file.
  - #525: an Objective-C exception inside an agent's tool call crashes the app.
- **Cleanup:** the frozen test build and every lane worktree are removed. Your `creator-jobs` build caches are still there; that `rm` command is yours to run.

**Decisions that are yours:**
1. Fast-forward `main` to `worktree-help-docs`, and push? It's 22 commits: the docs site plus all the fixes.
2. Does `docs/site/` replace `docs/guide/`? Until it does, every change has to edit both.
3. Where will the site be hosted? Its `site` setting stays unset until you choose.
